entries.reason: votes a player nobody discussed or suspected all day (out-of-nowhere target); distinct from a silent bandwagon on the day's focus.
hinges on being named an investigate/protect target (private-role framing) plus a generic abstain; not a clean binary per player.
lurks silently through discussion then abstains with the majority; passive-abstain move, checkable from transcript + vote record.
preaches evidence/restraint over rash accusations then casts an elimination vote; canonical stated-principle-vs-vote contradiction.
spent discussion demanding justification for accusations against a player, then votes that same player; defend-then-flip.
actively argued against a specific target then abstains rather than following through on the attack.
the primary accused abstains instead of counter-voting an alternative or the accuser.
maintains vote on a target after the target visibly defended themselves; distinct from voter-side flips.
core checkable move is voting a player without any voiced suspicion in the immediate discussion; prior-ally storyline is incidental.
litigates one player's action/vote history then votes them; targeted record-attack-then-vote.
abstained the prior day on caution grounds then votes today; cross-day reversal from caution, different moments than vote_3.
votes a player who had publicly declared hesitation about voting; punishes prior vote-reluctance.
votes the day's focus target without ever voicing suspicion; silent bandwagon, absorbs the many rephrasings.
casts an explicit tie-breaker vote after previously abstaining on a tie; recurring tie mechanism, not one game's story.
reciprocates a vote against whoever just voted for them; trigger is a vote (not a verbal accusation), sibling of vote_15.
votes the player publicly accusing/challenging them; retaliatory vote against a verbal accuser (large merge cluster).
voting for the person you directly accused is the baseline consistent follow-through nearly all accusers exhibit; no discrimination.
argues the group should abstain citing insufficient information; verbal pro-abstain advocacy.
endorsing the abstain policy while warning against future inaction is the same pro-abstain advocacy move.
voting an accuser who attacked your voting record is a narrower trigger of the same retaliate-against-accuser move.
voting an off-focus player the discussion wasn't centered on is the same surprise-vote-on-non-central-target instance a reader would count.
criticizing/interrogating a player's past voting record then voting them is the same targeted record-litigation-then-vote.
voting a player after previously defending them is the same defend-then-flip move as vote_4.
voting an accuser who declared intent to eliminate you is the same retaliate-against-accuser move.
proposes a concrete vote-threshold mechanism against the room's preference to wait; procedural rule proposal.
strong preference against voting now (watch behavior instead) is the same argue-against-voting-now advocacy.
rejects another's suspicion methodology as too subjective and offers an alternative; reject-and-replace, distinct from bare proposal.
'monitor players who steer discussion toward voting criteria rather than observing silence' is too abstract to binary-check per player.
demands a decisive vote to avoid confusion then abstains; procedural-urging-then-abstain hypocrisy.
urging the group to study voting patterns then abstaining is the same advocate-engagement-then-abstain move.
voting someone who accused you of bloc coordination is a narrower trigger of retaliate-against-accuser.
merely asks the group to interpret a candidate's record (feigned neutrality, no stated suspicion) then votes them.
calling for a vote on a player then casting it is the same consistent-accusation-then-vote baseline as vote_16.
voices agreement with another's arguments then switches to their proposed target; adopts an ally's lead (voiced, unlike silent bandwagon).
votes the player leading the charge against them; retaliate-against-accuser under heavy storyline detail.
defined by a specific storyline (defended voters of the player revealed on death as investigator); would never recur as described.
openly advocates targeting a group of abstainers then votes one; advocacy-plus-execution, sibling of vote_11.
repeatedly pushes to break a prolonged deadlock then votes; deadlock-breaker move recurs across games.
accusing a player of a coordinated bloc then voting them is the same accuse-then-vote follow-through.
matching an accusatory leader's vote with minimal independent justification is the same silent bandwagon.
warns the group to be careful about assumptions/missing threats then abstains; caution-then-abstain, distinct trigger from vote_28.
dismissing a player's priorities as a distraction then voting them is an accuse/attack-then-vote instance.
espousing a discussion-framing principle (focus present-over-past) then voting is the same stated-principle-vs-vote move.
voting the accuser while labeling their accusation a survival play is retaliate-against-accuser plus verbal framing.
makes a role claim while demanding another's elimination; distinct claim-plus-push discussion move.
expressed skepticism, asked for more info, then votes that player; questioning-then-commit, sibling of vote_31/60.
repeatedly questions the timing of a late-game role claim; distinct meta-challenge move.
advocating a quantitative vote threshold to prevent splits is the same procedural threshold proposal as vote_24.
proposes a criterion for spotting suspicious behavior before voting; forward-looking suspicion rule.
announcing a voting-behavior condition to monitor during the vote is the same pre-vote suspicion-criterion proposal.
casts the sole non-abstain vote when the room agreed to avoid voting; lone-defector move.
warning against lynching quiet players then abstaining is the same voice-caution-then-abstain move.
warns against group-driven/herd voting then joins the consensus vote; anti-bandwagon-then-bandwagons, distinct from evidence-caution.
casts the vote while explicitly acknowledging it might be wrong; verbal hedge-while-voting, a distinct tell.
an accused player abstaining under an active accusation is the same accused-abstains move as vote_6.
flagging the push's speed as possible manipulation then joining it is the same warn-against-herd-then-join move.
initiating a suspicion line then immediately voting that player is the same accuse-then-vote follow-through.
raises a group-wide voting-speed comparison then votes the consensus target; comparative-record-then-bandwagon, distinct from single-player litigation.
suggesting comparison of current vs past voting speed then voting consensus is the same comparative-record move.
reviewing past voting sequences/hesitation then voting consensus is the same comparative-record-then-bandwagon.
asks both parties for justification (neutral arbiter) then votes one; arbiter-then-commit, sibling of vote_31/45.
accusing a player of driving a prior elimination then voting them is an accuse-then-vote instance.
voting the player who just accused you of driving a prior elimination is retaliate-against-accuser.
